name: Opposite Sharp Two-Arm Wings Require an Overlap of Order at Least Ten
statement: If both relative wings of an ample two-layer family attain equality in the two-arm holonomy bound, then their common section $B$ has at least ten concepts. Equivalently, opposite sharp two-arm systems cannot coexist over an overlap of order at most nine.
proof: If $|B|\le9$, either sharp wing writes the one-inclusion graph of $B$ as a connected active core of order $|B|-6\in\{1,2,3\}$ with two pendant length-three arms. The small-core uniqueness theorem forces the two wing decompositions of the same tree to have the same unordered arm pair. An arm's square support is the pair of coordinate labels on its attachment and terminal edges, so the two wings would have the same two support pairs. This contradicts the opposite-wing theorem that all four supports are distinct.
